deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a library loan slip (Leihschein), almost certainly from the Göttingen University Library. It records Bernhard Riemann borrowing S. F. Lacroix, 'Traité du calcul différentiel et du calcul intégral', volumes 1, 2 and 3.

The parts of the slip:
- **Ink header (Riemann's hand):** 'Lacroix. Traité du calcul différentiel et du calcul intégral. Tomes 1. 2. 3.' He first wrote 'intégral' after 'calcul', struck it through, and wrote 'différentiel' above it.
- **Pencil lines (librarian's hand):** a shelf or bibliographic check reading 'T. 1. 2. 3. Ed. 2' and 'Par. 1810', meaning the second edition, Paris, whose first volume appeared in 1810. Volumes 2 and 3 of that edition appeared in 1814 and 1819.
- **Pencil 'Zu' and large flourish:** probably a librarian's initial or check mark.
- **Lower-right signature:** 'B Riemann, Dr. ph.', followed by an address in parentheses.
- **Red-ink date:** 'Oct. 21. 54.', i.e. 21 October 1854. This is shortly after Riemann's Habilitation (June 1854), at the start of his career as a Privatdozent. He began lecturing on partial differential equations in the winter semester 1854/55, and borrowing Lacroix's comprehensive treatise fits course preparation.
- **'39':** the folio number of the archive.

There is no derivation to reconstruct.

results.what: Library loan record: Riemann borrowed Lacroix's Traité du calcul différentiel et du calcul intégral (2nd ed., 3 vols., Paris 1810–1819) on 21 Oct 1854

deep.surprise_reason: This is a book-loan slip with no mathematical content. It is of minor biographical interest only, documenting Riemann's reading while preparing his first lectures in 1854.
transcription_corrections: 'Zu[?]' is a large pencil librarian's mark or flourish, not part of the text.
'BRiemann, Dr. ph.' is correct (B. Riemann, Dr. phil.).
The parenthetical address '(Grosshzgl.[?] Agel[?])' is more plausibly a Göttingen street address, possibly '(Barfüßerstr. …)', followed by a name or house designation; it remains uncertain.
'Par. 1810.' is in the librarian's pencil and refers to the 2nd edition, Paris, vol. 1 1810 (vols. 2–3 in 1814 and 1819).
